5:20.ar: وَإِذۡ قَالَ مُوسَىٰ لِقَوۡمِهِۦ يَٰقَوۡمِ ٱذۡكُرُواْ نِعۡمَةَ ٱللَّهِ عَلَيۡكُمۡ إِذۡ جَعَلَ فِيكُمۡ أَنۢبِيَآءَ وَجَعَلَكُم مُّلُوكࣰ ا وَءَاتَىٰكُم مَّا لَمۡ يُؤۡتِ أَحَدࣰ ا مِّنَ ٱلۡعَٰلَمِينَ
5:20.en: And (remember) when Moses said unto his people: O my people! Remember Allah's favour unto you, how He placed among you prophets, and He made you kings, and gave you that (which) He gave not to any (other) of (His) creatures

5:21.ar: يَٰقَوۡمِ ٱدۡخُلُواْ ٱلۡأَرۡضَ ٱلۡمُقَدَّسَةَ ٱلَّتِي كَتَبَ ٱللَّهُ لَكُمۡ وَلَا تَرۡتَدُّواْ عَلَىٰٓ أَدۡبَارِكُمۡ فَتَنقَلِبُواْ خَٰسِرِينَ
5:21.en: O my people! Go into the holy land which Allah hath ordained for you. Turn not in flight, for surely ye turn back as losers

5:22.ar: قَالُواْ يَٰمُوسَىٰٓ إِنَّ فِيهَا قَوۡمࣰ ا جَبَّارِينَ وَإِنَّا لَن نَّدۡخُلَهَا حَتَّىٰ يَخۡرُجُواْ مِنۡهَا فَإِن يَخۡرُجُواْ مِنۡهَا فَإِنَّا دَٰخِلُونَ
5:22.en: They said: O Moses! Lo! a giant people (dwell) therein and lo! we go not in till they go forth from thence. When they go forth from thence, then we will enter (not till then)

5:23.ar: قَالَ رَجُلَانِ مِنَ ٱلَّذِينَ يَخَافُونَ أَنۡعَمَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيۡهِمَا ٱدۡخُلُواْ عَلَيۡهِمُ ٱلۡبَابَ فَإِذَا دَخَلۡتُمُوهُ فَإِنَّكُمۡ غَٰلِبُونَۚ وَعَلَى ٱللَّهِ فَتَوَكَّلُوٓاْ إِن كُنتُم مُّؤۡمِنِينَ
5:23.en: Then out spake two of those who feared (their Lord, men) unto whom Allah had been gracious: Enter in upon them by the gate, for if ye enter by it, lo! ye will be victorious. So put your trust (in Allah) if ye are indeed believers

5:24.ar: قَالُواْ يَٰمُوسَىٰٓ إِنَّا لَن نَّدۡخُلَهَآ أَبَدࣰ ا مَّا دَامُواْ فِيهَا فَٱذۡهَبۡ أَنتَ وَرَبُّكَ فَقَٰتِلَآ إِنَّا هَٰهُنَا قَٰعِدُونَ
5:24.en: They said: O Moses! We will never enter (the land) while they are in it. So go thou and thy Lord and fight! We will sit here

5:25.ar: قَالَ رَبِّ إِنِّي لَآ أَمۡلِكُ إِلَّا نَفۡسِي وَأَخِيۖ فَٱفۡرُقۡ بَيۡنَنَا وَبَيۡنَ ٱلۡقَوۡمِ ٱلۡفَٰسِقِينَ
5:25.en: He said: My Lord! I have control of none but myself and my brother, so distinguish between us and the wrong-doing folk

5:26.ar: قَالَ فَإِنَّهَا مُحَرَّمَةٌ عَلَيۡهِمۡۛ أَرۡبَعِينَ سَنَةࣰۛ يَتِيهُونَ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِۚ فَلَا تَأۡسَ عَلَى ٱلۡقَوۡمِ ٱلۡفَٰسِقِينَ
5:26.en: (Their Lord) said: For this the land will surely be forbidden them for forty years that they will wander in the earth, bewildered. So grieve not over the wrongdoing folk

5:54.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ مَن يَرۡتَدَّ مِنكُمۡ عَن دِينِهِۦ فَسَوۡفَ يَأۡتِي ٱللَّهُ بِقَوۡمࣲ يُحِبُّهُمۡ وَيُحِبُّونَهُۥٓ أَذِلَّةٍ عَلَى ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ أَعِزَّةٍ عَلَى ٱلۡكَٰفِرِينَ يُجَٰهِدُونَ فِي سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ وَلَا يَخَافُونَ لَوۡمَةَ لَآئِمࣲۚ ذَٰلِكَ فَضۡلُ ٱللَّهِ يُؤۡتِيهِ مَن يَشَآءُۚ وَٱللَّهُ وَٰسِعٌ عَلِيمٌ
5:54.en: O ye who believe! Whoso of you becometh a renegade from his religion, (know that in his stead) Allah will bring a people whom He loveth and who love Him, humble toward believers, stern toward disbelievers, striving in the way of Allah, and fearing not the blame of any blamer. Such is the grace of Allah which He giveth unto whom He will. Allah is All-Embracing, All-Knowing

5:105.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ عَلَيۡكُمۡ أَنفُسَكُمۡۖ لَا يَضُرُّكُم مَّن ضَلَّ إِذَا ٱهۡتَدَيۡتُمۡۚ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ مَرۡجِعُكُمۡ جَمِيعࣰ ا فَيُنَبِّئُكُم بِمَا كُنتُمۡ تَعۡمَلُونَ
5:105.en: O ye who believe! Ye have charge of your own souls. He who erreth cannot injure you if ye are rightly guided. Unto Allah ye will all return; and then He will inform you of what ye used to do

47:38.ar: هَٰٓأَنتُمۡ هَٰٓؤُلَآءِ تُدۡعَوۡنَ لِتُنفِقُواْ فِي سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ فَمِنكُم مَّن يَبۡخَلُۖ وَمَن يَبۡخَلۡ فَإِنَّمَا يَبۡخَلُ عَن نَّفۡسِهِۦۚ وَٱللَّهُ ٱلۡغَنِيُّ وَأَنتُمُ ٱلۡفُقَرَآءُۚ وَإِن تَتَوَلَّوۡاْ يَسۡتَبۡدِلۡ قَوۡمًا غَيۡرَكُمۡ ثُمَّ لَا يَكُونُوٓاْ أَمۡثَٰلَكُم
47:38.en: Lo! ye are those who are called to spend in the way of Allah, yet among you there are some who hoard. And as for him who hoardeth, he hoardeth only from his soul. And Allah is the Rich, and ye are the poor. And if ye turn away He will exchange you for some other folk, and they will not be the likes of you

2:165.ar: وَمِنَ ٱلنَّاسِ مَن يَتَّخِذُ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ أَندَادࣰ ا يُحِبُّونَهُمۡ كَحُبِّ ٱللَّهِۖ وَٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓاْ أَشَدُّ حُبࣰّ ا لِّلَّهِۗ وَلَوۡ يَرَى ٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوٓاْ إِذۡ يَرَوۡنَ ٱلۡعَذَابَ أَنَّ ٱلۡقُوَّةَ لِلَّهِ جَمِيعࣰ ا وَأَنَّ ٱللَّهَ شَدِيدُ ٱلۡعَذَابِ
2:165.en: Yet of mankind are some who take unto themselves (objects of worship which they set as) rivals to Allah, loving them with a love like (that which is the due) of Allah (only) - those who believe are stauncher in their love for Allah - Oh, that those who do evil had but known, (on the day) when they behold the doom, that power belongeth wholly to Allah, and that Allah is severe in punishment

8:25.ar: وَٱتَّقُواْ فِتۡنَةࣰ لَّا تُصِيبَنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُواْ مِنكُمۡ خَآصَّةࣰۖ وَٱعۡلَمُوٓاْ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ شَدِيدُ ٱلۡعِقَابِ
8:25.en: And guard yourselves against a chastisement which cannot fall exclusively on those of you who are wrong-doers, and know that Allah is severe in punishment

0qgfFqeBm1I.title: Ramadan 2025, Night 6: Quranic Themes, Obeying Allah
0qgfFqeBm1I.one_line: Obedience through al-Ma'idah: Bani Israel's refusal and forty lost years, the people Allah brings in place of the disobedient, and 'you are responsible for yourselves'.
0qgfFqeBm1I.summary: He separates obedience from submission: Islam means surrendering part of one's will to Allah, while obedience is part of all life, owed at work and at home, and owed above all to Allah. When Musa told Bani Israel to enter the holy land, they refused out of fear of its strong inhabitants, rejected the promise that pushing the gate would bring victory, and told Musa to go fight with his Lord. Allah kept them wandering forty years until a generation passed, so even Musa and Harun never entered, and a new generation under a new leader took Jerusalem. He draws two lessons: disobedience risks Allah giving up on you, and dua must ask Him to bless our own effort rather than hand Him the work He assigned us, like praying for unity while dividing. Verse 5:54 warns that whoever turns away will be replaced by a people He loves who love Him, humble with believers, firm with enemies, striving, and unafraid of any blamer; he stresses wisdom but insists Allah's command must outweigh status or fear at life's forks. Verse 5:105 does not excuse abandoning others: Abu Bakr corrected that reading, the prophets feared collective punishment, and only after doing everything possible is one answerable for oneself alone, as the Prophet told his own family.

outline.heading: Obedience is not the same as submission
outline.gist: Islam is giving up part of your free will for Allah, so heavy an ask that the religion is named after it; obedience is part of ordinary life, to a boss or to parents, and the idea of obeying no one is silly.

outline.heading: A canvas theme
outline.gist: Some surahs focus on obedience specifically, but as an underlying theme it is encouraged everywhere in the Quran and its opposite warned against.

outline.heading: Interlude
Musa: remember Allah's favour and enter the land
outline.gist: After crossing the sea, Musa reminds his people that Allah gave them prophets, kings and bounty no one else in the region had, and commands them to enter the holy land written for them and not turn back.

outline.heading: Not until they leave
outline.gist: The land was held by a mighty people, so Bani Israel answered that they would not enter or lose lives until its inhabitants left.

outline.heading: Just push the gate
outline.gist: Two God-fearing men told them to enter the gate and they would win; Allah was not bargaining but offering a discount, removing their fear with a guarantee.

outline.heading: You and your Lord go and fight
outline.gist: They refused while the enemy remained, twice their size and number, and told Musa that if his Lord guaranteed it, he and his Lord should fight while they waited behind.

outline.heading: Forty years of wandering
outline.gist: Musa pleads that he has only himself and his brother and asks to be separated from the defiant; the land is forbidden to them for forty years of wandering, and he is told not to grieve for them.

outline.heading: Musa never reached the holy land
outline.gist: Musa and Harun both died during those years, so two great prophets destined to live there were deprived of it because their people disobeyed.

outline.heading: A generation replaced
outline.gist: In forty years a congregation changes completely, as he notes of himself and the children running about; Musa and Harun turned to raising the next generation, which produced a leader and a prophet who reclaimed Jerusalem.

outline.heading: The risk of Allah giving up on you
outline.gist: When people do not obey, Allah may deem them unworthy of victory and honour and wait for the next generation to offer it again.

outline.heading: Dua is asking for aid, not delegation
outline.gist: When we pray for the ummah's victory or unity we must mean 'aid me as I work for it'; asking Allah to do what He commanded us to do while we wait is exactly what Bani Israel did.

outline.heading: Praying for unity while dividing
outline.gist: Asking for unity while actively splitting the ummah is like an unmarried young man praying for children: he should first find a wife and do his part, then make the dua.

outline.heading: Obedience: doing it even when it is scary
outline.gist: Obeying Allah means understanding what He expects and doing it even when it is frightening, uncertain or unlikely to work out.

outline.heading: Turning back: apostasy or refusal
outline.gist: Turning back from the faith can be open apostasy or simply refusing a command; in Allah's eyes refusal is a kind of turning away, though in jurisprudence the two are not the same.

outline.heading: We judge by declared faith, not by sins
outline.gist: No one speaks for Allah: whoever says the shahadah is Muslim unless he clearly rejects the Quran or the prophethood; confusing the two views breeds extremism, and Muslims debated the unrepentant major sinner for five centuries.

outline.heading: Allah will bring another people
outline.gist: Whoever turns back should know Allah will bring a different people, as Surah Muhammad states even more clearly: He will replace you and they will not be like you.

outline.heading: Fear being replaced; don't complain of your post
outline.gist: Starting with himself, everyone should fear that Allah could pluck him out and bring someone better; whoever has been placed to do good should do it without complaint.

outline.heading: He loves them and they love Him
outline.gist: Allah loved the group He replaced too; what changes is that the new people love Him back.

outline.heading: Believers love Allah the most
outline.gist: Some love idols or worldly things as one should love God, but believers love Allah more than anything; the first quality of the obedient is that love.

outline.heading: Love already shown to you
outline.gist: That you are in His house, a Muslim, hearing a reminder and about to pray is love enough for infinite lifetimes; what remains is to return it.

outline.heading: Humble toward the believers
outline.gist: They carry humility in their hearts toward their fellow believers.

outline.heading: Mighty against their enemies
outline.gist: They are not weak or afraid before their enemies and do not sell out.

outline.heading: Striving in Allah's path
outline.gist: They strive for the sake of Allah.

outline.heading: No fear of any blamer
outline.gist: When Allah commands, they obey without weighing what people will say or how their social, financial or academic standing will shift; this is why he chose the verse.

outline.heading: Wisdom, but a fork in the road
outline.gist: Obeying Allah does not mean getting yourself fired or offending people needlessly, yet everyone meets a moment where it is Allah's command or another consideration, and fearing something else more is the danger.

outline.heading: The fifth quality is the one that matters
outline.gist: You may love Allah, be humble, firm and striving, but without the fifth you can still be replaced; his point is not to lose jobs and ask the masjid for work, but to let Allah's direct command come first even when it costs you.

outline.heading: Most commands cost nothing, a few are tests
outline.gist: Nine in ten commands will never threaten your livelihood or status, but a few tests will, and Allah promises to replace those who turn back with people better than them.

outline.heading: Why wait to be replaced?
outline.gist: We can choose to be those people now; Allah has done it before, letting a generation die off over forty years so that not one soldier in Yusha's army had been present at Musa's command.

outline.heading: You are responsible for yourselves
outline.gist: Al-Ma'idah is a surah of practical commands, with sixteen addresses to the believers; this unique one says to take care of yourselves, since those who stray cannot harm you if you are guided, and all return to Allah.

outline.heading: Cut-and-paste religion
outline.gist: The verse was taken out of context within a generation, which is why scholars and knowledge are needed; cherry-picking what one likes from the Quran and assembling a new religion is, in his understanding, the meaning of bid'ah.

outline.heading: Abu Bakr corrects a misreading
outline.gist: People began using the verse to drop dawah; Abu Bakr, a man who spoke rarely but decisively, as on the day the Prophet died and in his first address as caliph, stood up to correct them.

outline.heading: Command good or face collective punishment
outline.gist: He reported hearing the Prophet say that if people do not command good and forbid wrong, Allah will soon send a punishment covering everyone, like the trial that strikes more than the wrongdoers.

outline.heading: The army swallowed with its servants
outline.gist: The prophets feared that righteous individuals are not spared when a community is punished; an army that will march on the Ka'bah is swallowed whole, including those only feeding and serving it, and raised by their intentions.

outline.heading: Destroyed though the righteous are among them
outline.gist: Asked whether people can be destroyed while righteous people live among them, the Prophet said yes, when corruption far outweighs piety.

outline.heading: Read under the duty of dawah
outline.gist: Underlying themes like the obligation of dawah govern how a verse is read; Allah is consoling the one who calls tirelessly and is not heard, not excusing silence.

outline.heading: After you have done all you can
outline.gist: You must care for your community; only when every effort has failed to bring change does your responsibility narrow to yourself.

outline.heading: Answerable for those you could influence
outline.gist: You will be asked whether you tried with those you could reach; if you tried and were rejected each time, you are safe, and in the end you must save yourself.

outline.heading: Save yourselves: the Prophet to his family
outline.gist: At a second family feast, speaking while Abu Lahab's mouth was full, the Prophet told his uncle, his aunt and his daughter to save themselves from the Fire, offering Fatimah all his wealth but saying he could not avail her before Allah.

outline.heading: Obedience in summary
outline.gist: Obey by acting on His commands, ask Him for aid rather than delegation, know that the disobedient are replaced by those who put His command first, and remember that at the start and the end you answer for yourself.

outline.heading: Outro

6:59.ar: ۞وَعِندَهُۥ مَفَاتِحُ ٱلۡغَيۡبِ لَا يَعۡلَمُهَآ إِلَّا هُوَۚ وَيَعۡلَمُ مَا فِي ٱلۡبَرِّ وَٱلۡبَحۡرِۚ وَمَا تَسۡقُطُ مِن وَرَقَةٍ إِلَّا يَعۡلَمُهَا وَلَا حَبَّةࣲ فِي ظُلُمَٰتِ ٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَلَا رَطۡبࣲ وَلَا يَابِسٍ إِلَّا فِي كِتَٰبࣲ مُّبِينࣲ‏
6:59.en: And with Him are the keys of the Invisible. None but He knoweth them. And He knoweth what is in the land and the sea. Not a leaf falleth but He knoweth it, not a grain amid the darkness of the earth, naught of wet or dry but (it is noted) in a clear record

6:95.ar: ۞إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ فَالِقُ ٱلۡحَبِّ وَٱلنَّوَىٰۖ يُخۡرِجُ ٱلۡحَيَّ مِنَ ٱلۡمَيِّتِ وَمُخۡرِجُ ٱلۡمَيِّتِ مِنَ ٱلۡحَيِّۚ ذَٰلِكُمُ ٱللَّهُۖ فَأَنَّىٰ تُؤۡفَكُونَ
6:95.en: Lo! Allah (it is) Who splitteth the grain of corn and the date-stone (for sprouting). He bringeth forth the living from the dead, and is the bringer-forth of the dead from the living. Such is Allah. How then are ye perverted

6:96.ar: فَالِقُ ٱلۡإِصۡبَاحِ وَجَعَلَ ٱلَّيۡلَ سَكَنࣰ ا وَٱلشَّمۡسَ وَٱلۡقَمَرَ حُسۡبَانࣰ اۚ ذَٰلِكَ تَقۡدِيرُ ٱلۡعَزِيزِ ٱلۡعَلِيمِ
6:96.en: He is the Cleaver of the Daybreak, and He hath appointed the night for stillness, and the sun and the moon for reckoning. That is the measuring of the Mighty, the Wise

6:97.ar: وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِي جَعَلَ لَكُمُ ٱلنُّجُومَ لِتَهۡتَدُواْ بِهَا فِي ظُلُمَٰتِ ٱلۡبَرِّ وَٱلۡبَحۡرِۗ قَدۡ فَصَّلۡنَا ٱلۡأٓيَٰتِ لِقَوۡمࣲ يَعۡلَمُونَ
6:97.en: And He it is Who hath set for you the stars that ye may guide your course by them amid the darkness of the land and the sea. We have detailed Our revelations for a people who have knowledge

6:98.ar: وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِيٓ أَنشَأَكُم مِّن نَّفۡسࣲ وَٰحِدَةࣲ فَمُسۡتَقَرࣱّ وَمُسۡتَوۡدَعࣱۗ قَدۡ فَصَّلۡنَا ٱلۡأٓيَٰتِ لِقَوۡمࣲ يَفۡقَهُونَ
6:98.en: And He it is Who hath produced you from a single being, and (hath given you) a habitation and a repository. We have detailed Our revelations for a people who have understanding

6:99.ar: وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِيٓ أَنزَلَ مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ مَآءࣰ فَأَخۡرَجۡنَا بِهِۦ نَبَاتَ كُلِّ شَيۡءࣲ فَأَخۡرَجۡنَا مِنۡهُ خَضِرࣰ ا نُّخۡرِجُ مِنۡهُ حَبࣰّ ا مُّتَرَاكِبࣰ ا وَمِنَ ٱلنَّخۡلِ مِن طَلۡعِهَا قِنۡوَانࣱ دَانِيَةࣱ وَجَنَّٰتࣲ مِّنۡ أَعۡنَابࣲ وَٱلزَّيۡتُونَ وَٱلرُّمَّانَ مُشۡتَبِهࣰ ا وَغَيۡرَ مُتَشَٰبِهٍۗ ٱنظُرُوٓاْ إِلَىٰ ثَمَرِهِۦٓ إِذَآ أَثۡمَرَ وَيَنۡعِهِۦٓۚ إِنَّ فِي ذَٰلِكُمۡ لَأٓيَٰتࣲ لِّقَوۡمࣲ يُؤۡمِنُونَ
6:99.en: He it is Who sendeth down water from the sky, and therewith We bring forth buds of every kind; We bring forth the green blade from which We bring forth the thick-clustered grain; and from the date-palm, from the pollen thereof, spring pendant bunches; and (We bring forth) gardens of grapes, and the olive and the pomegranate, alike and unlike. Look upon the fruit thereof, when they bear fruit, and upon its ripening. Lo! herein verily are portents for a people who believe

sc14D5RJLCw.speaker: adnan

sc14D5RJLCw.title: Ramadan 2025, Night 7: Quranic Themes, Knowing Allah
sc14D5RJLCw.one_line: Knowing Allah, the Quran's foremost theme, through His total knowledge (6:59), His creation of all growth (6:95-99) and His vast mercy (6:147).
sc14D5RJLCw.summary: He ranks knowing Allah as the Quran's undisputed first theme, since every prophet's first task was to show people His signs so they would know Him. Our minds work within time and space, which Allah created, so His essence is beyond us; the Quran describes Him through analogies while warning that He is not like us. Human mercy runs through contemplation and empathy, but Allah created the very concepts of mercy and knowledge, so none can exceed Him in them. Because He cannot be seen, heard or pictured like a person, this relationship depends on precise description, and truly knowing Him brings a reverence and love that would end sin. Verse 6:59, the keys of the unseen and every falling leaf and hidden grain, shows knowledge both general and detailed; he says he would not worship a God who could be surprised. Verses 6:95-99 present Allah as splitter of seed and dawn and the One who brings forth the growth of everything from water and soil; he finds a shared origin of life beautiful rather than threatening, and insists that understanding how something works never removes its Maker. Verse 6:147 tells the Prophet to answer hostile rejecters first with Allah's vast mercy, the hundred mercies and the nature of ar-Rahman, while reminding them His punishment is not turned back.

outline.heading: The number one theme
outline.gist: Ranked by importance and recurrence, knowing Allah comes first, and the Quran itself confirms it: the prophets' first task was to recite His signs so that people would know Him.

outline.heading: Beyond time and space
outline.gist: We can only fully comprehend what exists in time and space and can be measured; Allah created both and is not bound by them, so simple logic tells us His essence is beyond our tools.

outline.heading: Knowing Him within our limits
outline.gist: Some aspects of Allah are unfathomable, but the Quran explains a great deal in terms and analogies we understand, while He remains unlike His creation.

outline.heading: Mercy: the same word, not the same process
outline.gist: Human mercy comes from contemplating someone's struggle and feeling empathy; that is not how Allah shows mercy, and since He created the concept itself, no one can surpass Him in it.

outline.heading: Knowledge is His creation
outline.gist: He created knowledge and the brain that processes it, so claiming some part of knowledge escapes Him is absurd.

outline.heading: Analogies to understand and emulate
outline.gist: The Quran's similes help us grasp who He is and emulate the attributes He wants us to; whoever truly knows Him will not struggle to obey.

outline.heading: A relationship without the senses
outline.gist: We know people by seeing, hearing, even smelling them, and can picture a grandfather we never met or the Prophet from descriptions, but no relationship is like the one with Allah.

outline.heading: Precise description, reverence and love
outline.gist: This relationship needs delicate, accurate description, which the Quran gives; reverence and love built on it would solve every crisis in a person's life.

outline.heading: The biggest hurdle
outline.gist: Great scholars were called 'one who knows Allah'; knowledge of the sciences of religion is pointless without knowing and revering Him.

outline.heading: The keys of the unseen
outline.gist: Only Allah holds the keys to the realm we cannot access beyond what He reveals, and He knows all that is on land and in the sea.

outline.heading: Not a leaf falls without His knowledge
outline.gist: Countless leaves have fallen throughout history and every one is known in detail; the verse moves from a general statement to the particular so that no one wonders whether He knows what happens to him.

outline.heading: A grain in the darkness of the earth
outline.gist: No grain in the deepest darkness, nothing living or dead, escapes a clear record, beyond the reach of any instrument we have.

outline.heading: Our distinction is learning; His knowledge is total
outline.gist: What makes humans unique is our capacity to learn, and Allah knows not only what we gather but everything that can be known.

outline.heading: Even what never happened
outline.gist: Scholars add that He knows what was, is and will be, and what did not happen and how it would have unfolded if it had, a theme he will treat later.

outline.heading: If you can be surprised, you can be beaten
outline.gist: He would not devote his worship to anyone not all-knowing, because any ignorance, however small, means the possibility of being surprised and therefore defeated.

outline.heading: Shaytan's whisper: how does He know?
outline.gist: We learn by trial, steering the car into the wall or pressing enter on code, and then measure Allah's knowledge by ours; He owns knowledge itself.

outline.heading: Splitter of seed and dawn
outline.gist: Allah splits the grain and seed, brings the living from the dead and the dead from the living, breaks the dawn, makes the night for rest and the sun and moon for reckoning time.

outline.heading: Not like dealing with a king
outline.gist: The verses describing Allah move him most; whoever deals with Him like a person of status misses that He is the King of kings, and seeing Him rightly brings humility, devotion and trust however dark things get.

outline.heading: Stars to navigate by
outline.gist: He placed the stars for guidance on land and sea, signs laid out for those with knowledge.

outline.heading: From a single soul
outline.gist: He created all people from one soul, with a place to settle and a place of deposit, signs for those who reflect.

outline.heading: The growth of everything
outline.gist: From rain He brings forth the nabat of everything; the word means growth, used for knowledge growing between people or a young person growing up, not only plants.

outline.heading: Green, grain and fruit
outline.gist: First comes green, then grain layered on grain, clusters of dates hanging low, gardens of grapes, olives and pomegranates alike in look yet different in taste; watch the fruit as it ripens.

outline.heading: A shared origin with all life
outline.gist: We all grew from the earth; why be offended at sharing an origin and DNA with a tree, when one self-correcting code producing all life is breathtaking?

outline.heading: We create nothing; we only imitate
outline.gist: Show me what anyone besides Allah created: we copied the falcon for planes, the duck for boats and the cell's code for algorithms, poorly; for Him it was simple, water from the sky and a little green.

outline.heading: Knowing how does not remove the Maker
outline.gist: Seeing how sperm and egg meet or how grafting makes new fruit makes creation more miraculous, not less; science explaining a process does not mean Allah did not set it in motion.

outline.heading: We only work within His framework
outline.gist: If a watered seed in the sun refuses to grow or a body stops despite every treatment, we have nothing; discovering gravity does not mean no one placed it, and treating understanding as disproof shows a failure to grasp what one studies.

outline.heading: Say: your Lord is of vast mercy
outline.gist: When people reject the Prophet completely, the first thing he is told to say is that their Lord's mercy is the widest of all.

outline.heading: A hundred mercies
outline.gist: When Allah created the heavens and earth He created a hundred mercies; Allah created the very concept, so this is not an analogy.

outline.heading: The one mercy we share
outline.gist: He sent one of them to earth, and through it we feel empathy, give and protect one another, and an animal lifts its hoof from its young; we do not use up even that share.

outline.heading: When all hundred are spread
outline.gist: On the Day of Judgment the remaining mercy is joined to the ninety-nine and spread over creation; a narration of uncertain strength says even Iblis will raise his head in hope, though he made his choice long ago.

outline.heading: The name the Quraysh resisted
outline.gist: The disbelievers could not accept the name ar-Rahman, which was so beautiful that people embraced Islam just by hearing it explained.

outline.heading: Ar-Rahman: mercy as His constant nature
outline.gist: Rahim implies mercy with a cause and a deserving recipient, while the pattern of Rahman, like a word for someone always hungry rather than hungry for one meal, describes a constant, innate quality.

outline.heading: Yet His punishment is not turned back
outline.gist: His punishment cannot be averted from the criminals, but because His nature is Rahman everyone receives some of His mercy, which is why people were drawn to this description.

outline.heading: Mercy encompasses everything
outline.gist: Elsewhere He says His mercy encompasses every thing, living or not, human or not, Muslim or not, and on His Throne it is written that His mercy precedes His wrath.

outline.heading: Why you come every night
outline.gist: Even toward those actively fighting the truth the Prophet is told to begin with mercy; we come each night because we already have the mercy of Rahman and want the special mercy of Rahim given to those He loves, while knowing His punishment is real.

outline.heading: Knowledge, creation, mercy and wrath
outline.gist: Know that He is all-knowing in general and in detail, that He created everything with purpose and you are part of it, and that He is most compassionate yet also punishes, so cling to His mercy while fearing His wrath.

Fcm5NRYRvE4.title: Tazkiyah Pearls 6: The Soul, the Cycle and the Qalb (Subconscious)
Fcm5NRYRvE4.one_line: How the nafs works and is tamed, the conscience, the thought-action-feeling cycle, and changing feelings by changing what enters the heart.
Fcm5NRYRvE4.summary: He deepens the picture of the nafs: made from the earth, it is programmed for survival and superiority, indifferent to whether means are lawful, unaware of what is truly good for you, unwilling to act unless there is something in it for itself, and unable to accept delayed reward, much like a selfish toddler. Many of its convictions, such as believing you deserve good things, should be kept but rewired to the right source; those whose nafs lost that belief through abuse need therapy. The goal is to tame the nafs, not break it, and he describes five levels for each behaviour, from total surrender to the nafs through a seesaw, forced compliance and resigned habit, to agreement. The conscience is the ruh's influence on the nafs, and its death is the beginning of death. He then presents the cycle in which thoughts, actions and feelings shape one another: we control our actions fully, our thoughts partly through reflection, and our feelings not at all. A Damascene story of a woman who set out to poison her mother-in-law with nightly massages shows good actions changing hatred into love. Feelings come from the heart's mixing pot of what we see, hear, think and are surrounded by, so he asks listeners to change their inputs and expectations patiently, since tazkiyah is slow.

outline.heading: Opening
The nafs is programmed for survival
outline.gist: Coming from the soil of the earth, the nafs, like all life, wants to survive, dominate and take in the most energy for the least effort.

outline.heading: It cares about outcomes, not means
outline.gist: Halal or haram means nothing to it; it loves you but does not know what is best, which is why domesticated animals and people overeat.

outline.heading: There must be something in it for the nafs
outline.gist: Selflessness is hard because the nafs resists anything that profits it nothing, such as strengthening someone else; it is not evil, just programmed, so we do not hate it.

outline.heading: No delayed reward: a toddler inside
outline.gist: A bird in the hand beats ten in the tree; the nafs trusts no one and is a selfish child we carry within.

outline.heading: Keep its convictions, change the reasons
outline.gist: Believing you deserve good things is essential and should be rewired to Allah as its source; those whose nafs lost it through abuse need real therapy.

outline.heading: Tame the nafs, do not break it
outline.gist: A broken nafs leaves a person without integrity or courage; taming happens in levels.

outline.heading: Level one: no resistance
outline.gist: Like a parent who gives a two-year-old everything, the person simply submits to whatever the nafs wants.

outline.heading: Level two: the seesaw
outline.gist: Some days you win and some days the nafs wins; your level differs for each behaviour.

outline.heading: Level three: forcing the nafs
outline.gist: The nafs hates it but has no choice, as with most people going to work or sometimes to Fajr.

outline.heading: Level four: the nafs gives up
outline.gist: It stops fighting and the act becomes habit, though without passion and with the nafs still thinking it wasteful.

outline.heading: Level five: the nafs agrees
outline.gist: As in play, the nafs wants what you want; the hope is to reach this for the deeds that bring us close to Allah.

outline.heading: The conscience: the ruh's effect on the nafs
outline.gist: The stronger the spirit's influence on the nafs, the stronger the conscience; it is one nafs with different states.

outline.heading: The death of the conscience
outline.gist: Death begins when the spirit no longer influences the nafs; a good upbringing, environment and values of compassion strengthen the spirit.

outline.heading: Connection to Allah as an endless source
outline.gist: Those good before Islam became good in Islam; without a link to Allah the spirit shrivels and needs constant upkeep.

outline.heading: The cycle of thoughts, actions and feelings
outline.gist: Each one affects and is affected by the other two, so the cycle is always virtuous or vicious.

outline.heading: How much of each we control
outline.gist: We control all our actions, a variable share of our thoughts that grows with contemplation, and none of our feelings directly.

outline.heading: Breaking a vicious cycle
outline.gist: Disliking someone breeds negative thoughts and bad actions that deepen the dislike; jam a rod in the wheel by deliberately thinking and acting well.

outline.heading: The mother-in-law and the poison lotion
outline.gist: A Damascene apothecary gave a woman plain lotion to massage her mother-in-law nightly; after twenty days she came back begging for an antidote because she now loved her.

outline.heading: Feelings are the strongest part of the cycle
outline.gist: Strong feelings power both thoughts and actions, raising the question of how to influence what we cannot control.

outline.heading: The qalb's four inputs
outline.gist: The heart mixes what we see, what we hear, our environment and our thoughts, and its output is our emotions.

outline.heading: The heart loves what it is fed, with a lag
outline.gist: Feeding it haram sights, sounds, company and thoughts makes it love haram; changes take months to show as old input filters out.

outline.heading: Turning a hated chore neutral through expectations
outline.gist: Taking out garbage or driving siblings feels awful when thought of negatively; treating it as a given makes the heart neutral about it.

outline.heading: Learning to enjoy what is not play, including salah
outline.gist: Changing outlook and associations can make a non-playful act joyful, which is how prayer moves from habit to enjoyment.

outline.heading: Tazkiyah is slow, not an aha moment
outline.gist: Few are granted a sudden transformation; most must identify their nafs and change thoughts and inputs to change behaviour over time.

outline.heading: Why everyone wants a front lawn
outline.gist: Our subconscious absorbed the background of films, so we want houses, cars and lawns without knowing why; change what you look at, listen to and surround yourself with.

outline.heading: Everything returns to this cycle
outline.gist: These simple principles let you take back control, changing how you feel about even tiring acts of worship.

gRx2E5Lyz7w.title: Tazkiyah Pearls 5: Deriving Self-Value
gRx2E5Lyz7w.one_line: Self-value is fixed by Allah, not earned; the pendulum between arrogance and low self-esteem, cutting false sources of worth, and healthier motivations.
gRx2E5Lyz7w.summary: After showing how the four daily focuses apply to a single deed, he calls self-value the most important topic in tazkiyah. He pictures a pendulum carried through life's bumps: success swings it toward vanity and arrogance, failure toward low self-esteem and inferiority, while the healthy middle combines confidence and humility. What swings it is deriving worth from changing sources. A Muslim's value is a fixed brick of gold granted by Allah, who honoured the children of Adam; praise cannot raise it nor contempt lower it, and all people are equal in it. Comparisons, achievements, wealth, status and even worship are cords the nafs attaches when we are not vigilant, and a pendulum that swings one way always swings back, which is why the arrogant are also insecure and why famous athletes and actors fall into depression when their careers end. Persistent low self-esteem, especially after trauma, calls for professional help. To the question of why act at all if worth is fixed, he answers that Muslims are moved by love, hope and fear, the bird and its two wings, and that one who keeps trying to prove his value cannot truly love. Feel good or bad about deeds, not about your worth, and never depend on deeds for salvation.

outline.heading: The four focuses applied to one deed
outline.gist: Intention before a deed, excellence during it, concern for acceptance after it, and asking whether it befits a servant; reflect on each daily, not for every act.

outline.heading: Why self-value comes first
outline.gist: Without a stable sense of self-value, its swings ruin every effort to draw closer to Allah, so it is the most important topic of tazkiyah.

outline.heading: The pendulum and the swing toward vanity
outline.gist: Life's bumps swing an inner pendulum; graduating, a new job or even scoring a goal can tip a person toward vanity and arrogance.

outline.heading: The opposite swing: low self-esteem
outline.gist: Illness, loss or repeated failure swing it toward feeling inferior; the healthy middle combines confidence and humility.

outline.heading: What makes the pendulum swing
outline.gist: It swings because people derive self-value from changing things; a true Muslim holds it firmly in the middle.

outline.heading: Self-value is fixed and divine
outline.gist: Your value is a constant brick from birth, given by Allah who honoured the children of Adam; a life spent proving value is how many of us were raised.

outline.heading: No one can touch it, and all are equal
outline.gist: Applause or spit changes nothing; this is truth, not self-deception, and asking why act at all if value is fixed is the saddest question.

outline.heading: Electric cords attached to the pendulum
outline.gist: Some people in the West are confident without needing to prove themselves; the pendulum swings because we draw value from sources other than Allah's constant word.

outline.heading: The comparison cord swings both ways
outline.gist: Feeling above others leads to feeling below them when they succeed, which is why arrogant people also carry inferiority.

outline.heading: The achievement cord, and cutting the cords
outline.gist: Missing a promotion or a job makes people feel less; cut every cord because value is divine and untouchable.

outline.heading: Prophets unmoved by love or humiliation
outline.gist: Whether paraded in honour or humiliated, their status as servants of Allah was unchanged.

outline.heading: The nafs attaches the cords
outline.gist: When vigilance drops, the nafs plugs in a new source because it wants the swing toward superiority, not realising the swing back is just as toxic.

outline.heading: When low self-esteem is stuck, seek help
outline.gist: Normally the nafs jerks the pendulum back from feeling low; if it stays stuck, mental health support is needed.

outline.heading: Not worship, wealth or status either
outline.gist: Worshipping more does not make you more human; bank balances and people's respect are false sources too.

outline.heading: Then why do anything?

outline.heading: Healthy motivation, and why value-seekers cannot love

4:94.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓاْ إِذَا ضَرَبۡتُمۡ فِي سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ فَتَبَيَّنُواْ وَلَا تَقُولُواْ لِمَنۡ أَلۡقَىٰٓ إِلَيۡكُمُ ٱلسَّلَٰمَ لَسۡتَ مُؤۡمِنࣰ ا تَبۡتَغُونَ عَرَضَ ٱلۡحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنۡيَا فَعِندَ ٱللَّهِ مَغَانِمُ كَثِيرَةࣱۚ كَذَٰلِكَ كُنتُم مِّن قَبۡلُ فَمَنَّ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيۡكُمۡ فَتَبَيَّنُوٓاْۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ كَانَ بِمَا تَعۡمَلُونَ خَبِيرࣰ ا
4:94.en: O ye who believe! When ye go forth (to fight) in the way of Allah, be careful to discriminate, and say not unto one who offereth you peace: "Thou art not a believer," seeking the chance profits of this life (so that ye may despoil him). With Allah are plenteous spoils. Even thus (as he now is) were ye before; but Allah hath since then been gracious unto you. Therefore take care to discriminate. Allah is ever Informed of what ye do

4:135.ar: ۞يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ كُونُواْ قَوَّٰمِينَ بِٱلۡقِسۡطِ شُهَدَآءَ لِلَّهِ وَلَوۡ عَلَىٰٓ أَنفُسِكُمۡ أَوِ ٱلۡوَٰلِدَيۡنِ وَٱلۡأَقۡرَبِينَۚ إِن يَكُنۡ غَنِيًّا أَوۡ فَقِيرࣰ ا فَٱللَّهُ أَوۡلَىٰ بِهِمَاۖ فَلَا تَتَّبِعُواْ ٱلۡهَوَىٰٓ أَن تَعۡدِلُواْۚ وَإِن تَلۡوُۥٓاْ أَوۡ تُعۡرِضُواْ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ كَانَ بِمَا تَعۡمَلُونَ خَبِيرࣰ ا
4:135.en: O ye who believe! Be ye staunch in justice, witnesses for Allah, even though it be against yourselves or (your) parents or (your) kindred, whether (the case be of) a rich man or a poor man, for Allah is nearer unto both (them ye are). So follow not passion lest ye lapse (from truth) and if ye lapse or fall away, then lo! Allah is ever Informed of what ye do

4:163.ar: ۞إِنَّآ أَوۡحَيۡنَآ إِلَيۡكَ كَمَآ أَوۡحَيۡنَآ إِلَىٰ نُوحࣲ وَٱلنَّبِيِّـۧنَ مِنۢ بَعۡدِهِۦۚ وَأَوۡحَيۡنَآ إِلَىٰٓ إِبۡرَٰهِيمَ وَإِسۡمَٰعِيلَ وَإِسۡحَٰقَ وَيَعۡقُوبَ وَٱلۡأَسۡبَاطِ وَعِيسَىٰ وَأَيُّوبَ وَيُونُسَ وَهَٰرُونَ وَسُلَيۡمَٰنَۚ وَءَاتَيۡنَا دَاوُۥدَ زَبُورࣰ ا
4:163.en: Lo! We inspire thee as We inspired Noah and the prophets after him, as We inspired Abraham and Ishmael and Isaac and Jacob and the tribes, and Jesus and Job and Jonah and Aaron and Solomon, and as We imparted unto David the Psalms

4:164.ar: وَرُسُلࣰ ا قَدۡ قَصَصۡنَٰهُمۡ عَلَيۡكَ مِن قَبۡلُ وَرُسُلࣰ ا لَّمۡ نَقۡصُصۡهُمۡ عَلَيۡكَۚ وَكَلَّمَ ٱللَّهُ مُوسَىٰ تَكۡلِيمࣰ ا
4:164.en: And messengers We have mentioned unto thee before and messengers We have not mentioned unto thee; and Allah spake directly unto Moses

4:165.ar: رُّسُلࣰ ا مُّبَشِّرِينَ وَمُنذِرِينَ لِئَلَّا يَكُونَ لِلنَّاسِ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ حُجَّةُۢ بَعۡدَ ٱلرُّسُلِۚ وَكَانَ ٱللَّهُ عَزِيزًا حَكِيمࣰ ا
4:165.en: Messengers of good cheer and of warning, in order that mankind might have no argument against Allah after the messengers. Allah was ever Mighty, Wise

4:166.ar: لَّٰكِنِ ٱللَّهُ يَشۡهَدُ بِمَآ أَنزَلَ إِلَيۡكَۖ أَنزَلَهُۥ بِعِلۡمِهِۦۖ وَٱلۡمَلَٰٓئِكَةُ يَشۡهَدُونَۚ وَكَفَىٰ بِٱللَّهِ شَهِيدًا
4:166.en: But Allah (Himself) testifieth concerning that which He hath revealeth unto thee; in His knowledge hath He revealed it; and the angels also testify. And Allah is sufficient Witness

41:20.ar: حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا مَا جَآءُوهَا شَهِدَ عَلَيۡهِمۡ سَمۡعُهُمۡ وَأَبۡصَٰرُهُمۡ وَجُلُودُهُم بِمَا كَانُواْ يَعۡمَلُونَ
41:20.en: Till, when they reach it, their ears and their eyes and their skins testify against them as to what they used to do

41:21.ar: وَقَالُواْ لِجُلُودِهِمۡ لِمَ شَهِدتُّمۡ عَلَيۡنَاۖ قَالُوٓاْ أَنطَقَنَا ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِيٓ أَنطَقَ كُلَّ شَيۡءࣲۚ وَهُوَ خَلَقَكُمۡ أَوَّلَ مَرَّةࣲ وَإِلَيۡهِ تُرۡجَعُونَ
41:21.en: And they say unto their skins: Why testify ye against us? They say: Allah hath given us speech Who giveth speech to all things, and Who created you at the first, and unto Whom ye are returned

41:22.ar: وَمَا كُنتُمۡ تَسۡتَتِرُونَ أَن يَشۡهَدَ عَلَيۡكُمۡ سَمۡعُكُمۡ وَلَآ أَبۡصَٰرُكُمۡ وَلَا جُلُودُكُمۡ وَلَٰكِن ظَنَنتُمۡ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يَعۡلَمُ كَثِيرࣰ ا مِّمَّا تَعۡمَلُونَ
41:22.en: Ye did not hide yourselves lest your ears and your eyes and your skins should testify against you, but ye deemed that Allah knew not much of what ye did

41:23.ar: وَذَٰلِكُمۡ ظَنُّكُمُ ٱلَّذِي ظَنَنتُم بِرَبِّكُمۡ أَرۡدَىٰكُمۡ فَأَصۡبَحۡتُم مِّنَ ٱلۡخَٰسِرِينَ
41:23.en: That, your thought which ye did think about your Lord, hath ruined you; and ye find yourselves (this day) among the lost

24ZV4JNepWc.title: Ramadan 2025, Night 5: Quranic Themes, Fairness and Justice
24ZV4JNepWc.one_line: Fairness as a major Quranic theme: toward people you once resembled (4:94), against yourself and your parents (4:135), and Allah's own fairness (4:163-166).
24ZV4JNepWc.summary: He calls fairness one of the Quran's major themes: between people, from Allah in this life and the next, and owed by us to Allah. Verse 4:94, a childhood favourite of his, tells soldiers on campaign to verify before acting and not to reject someone offering peace for the sake of spoils, which he links to Usama killing a man who had declared faith and the Prophet's repeated rebuke. Its heart is 'you were like them before': be fair to people where you once were, treating them as you were treated or wished to be, rather than holding them to a standard you did not meet, as elders who forget their own youth do with children in the masjid. Verse 4:135 asks believers to stand for justice even against themselves, their parents or relatives, which he admits is nearly impossible unless fairness outweighs every other value; he explains the layers of principle, ethic and application, the equality of all people, the Day of Judgment as the day of justice, and stopping a brother from oppressing. From 4:163-166 he argues that Allah sent prophets to every people so no one could plead ignorance, holding no one to account without fair warning. Each of us must therefore learn, teach and remove our liability before Allah as carefully as at work.

outline.heading: Themes as the alphabet of the Quran
outline.gist: A surah's purpose can be unique to it, while general themes such as trust in Allah's wisdom recur everywhere like letters forming words; memorising the month's themes gives you something to reflect on in any passage even when the surah's direction is unclear.

outline.heading: Fairness, a major theme
outline.gist: The Quran speaks of fairness between people, Allah's fairness now and on the Day of Judgment, and our fairness toward Allah; He oppresses no one, His creation must neither oppress nor accept oppression, and all of Islam's rulings aim at justice.

outline.heading: A verse from his childhood: setting out for battle
outline.gist: The verse stuck with him from youth; it addresses believers striding out on a campaign sent by the Prophet.

outline.heading: Verify and slow down
outline.gist: The command carries two meanings, seek clarification and do not be hasty: know what you are dealing with before deciding.

outline.heading: Salam as a declaration of peace
outline.gist: Do not tell someone who greets you with peace that he is not a believer; salam is a pledge that you will receive nothing but peace from me, which lets people coexist.

outline.heading: Even in war, not for the spoils
outline.gist: They were going out to fight, not to trade, yet were forbidden to doubt a man's declaration of peace out of desire for the spoils of an enemy.

outline.heading: Usama and the man who declared faith
outline.gist: After a long duel the man said there is no god but Allah as Usama's sword came down; the Prophet asked whether he had opened his heart to see, repeating 'you killed him after he said it' until Usama wished he had only just become Muslim.

outline.heading: Wanting the goods of this life
outline.gist: In the heat of battle it is easier to kill than to take a prisoner, and the motive is status, victory or wealth; Allah reminds them He has abundant bounty to give.

outline.heading: You were just like them once
outline.gist: There was a day you had no interest in faith, and Allah favoured you with guidance, so do not mount a high horse and bark at people for sins you only just stopped yourself.

outline.heading: Brought back gently, so be gentle
outline.gist: Most of us were not won back through harshness but by someone patient who found our hearts; fairness means treating the person in your old position the way you were treated.

outline.heading: The elder who forgot his own childhood
outline.gist: A man of sixty-five gave him constant trouble over the children in the masjid until his eighty-five-year-old uncle visited and told him what the man had been like as a boy, which silenced him for good.

outline.heading: Otherwise it is a double standard
outline.gist: If you were not treated well, ask how you would have wanted to be treated and do that; holding others to a standard you were never held to is a double standard, so hang this verse in your home.

outline.heading: Clarify before you judge
outline.gist: The parent who brings a very young child to the masjid may be a single parent, have a sick spouse at home or nowhere else to go; asking first may show they need your help.

outline.heading: The hallmark verse: principle, ethic, application
outline.gist: This is the verse to quote when showing Islam is about fairness; haqq is the principle, adl the ethic it produces, and qist its application, a key for following these words through the Quran.

outline.heading: Witness against yourself and your parents
outline.gist: Stand firmly for fairness as witnesses for Allah even against yourselves, your parents or relatives, a nearly impossible demand, since even those who manage it against themselves struggle against a parent.

outline.heading: The nightmare hypothetical
outline.gist: Imagine seeing a parent run someone over; you must at least answer the hypothetical rightly. Courts in North America do not force self-incrimination and spare close family in some cases precisely because most people would not testify, but this is what Allah commands.

outline.heading: When fairness outweighs everything
outline.gist: It becomes possible only when truth and justice outweigh every other value; he means the normal child who loves his parents and would take the fall for them, not someone who dislikes them.

outline.heading: Rich or poor, Allah is more worthy
outline.gist: Whether the person is wealthy or poor, Allah will take care of them; His command deserves to be followed more than worry over a loved one's welfare.

outline.heading: An implied threat in the ending
outline.gist: Do not follow desire away from justice; if you distort or turn away, Allah knows what you did and why, an implied threat of the kind found in most such verse endings.

outline.heading: The day of justice
outline.gist: The faith rests on no person being worth more than another, and the Day of Judgment exists because fairness is not always attainable here; for the oppressed it is their day, the danger is being on the wrong side of it.

outline.heading: The just leader of anything
outline.gist: Among those shaded by the Throne and whose prayers are answered is the just leader, which can mean the head of a school, company, hospital, masjid or household.

outline.heading: A verse the world quotes
outline.gist: The verse is cited internationally as a statement on justice; we are a nation willing to hold ourselves and our parents accountable when someone would otherwise be wronged.

outline.heading: Help your brother, oppressor or oppressed
outline.gist: You help an oppressor by stopping him and holding him to account, because evil left unchecked is a snowballing boomerang that returns to you, your family or your descendants.

outline.heading: Revelation as to Nuh and those after him
outline.gist: One of the verses listing the most prophets: Allah revealed to Muhammad as He revealed to Nuh, Ibrahim, Ismail, Ishaq, Yaqub and the tribes, Isa, Ayyub, Yunus, Harun and Sulayman, and gave Dawud the Psalms.

outline.heading: Prophets we have not told you about
outline.gist: Some prophets' stories we were told and others we were not; the large faiths that predate the Prophet suggest where they were.

outline.heading: Earlier faiths began with revelation
outline.gist: Judaism and Christianity were true when revealed, carrying the same teachings as the Quran, until human hands altered them; Muslims understand other ancient religions such as Hinduism and Buddhism to have begun the same way.

outline.heading: Parallels across isolated civilisations
outline.gist: Peoples who could never have met share a man and woman in a garden, a sin, resurrection, reward and punishment, and accountability, which only a common source explains.

outline.heading: Bearers of good news and warners
outline.gist: Allah spoke to Musa directly and sent messengers with the good news of His love and mercy and warnings of painful punishment.

outline.heading: So no one has an argument against Allah
outline.gist: No one can claim they never heard of Him; those who lived without access to any prophet are not held to the standard of faith, and how they are judged is left to Allah.

outline.heading: Whoever has the stronger argument
outline.gist: In any dispute the better argument wins; Allah will not hold accountable someone never properly taught, so He sent prophets with clear proofs to make accountability fair.

outline.heading: Allah bears witness to what He revealed
outline.gist: Allah and the angels witness what was revealed to the Prophet; you will never be held to an impossible standard, only to what you could do and learned of, so make sure you have a strong argument.

outline.heading: The teacher carries the blame for not teaching
outline.gist: If you were never properly taught, the one responsible for teaching you is accountable, which is why he must educate you; if you refuse to learn, it is on you.

outline.heading: Who blocked whom
outline.gist: In a charity or community, if those in charge prevent people from contributing, the blame falls on them; if they made it easy and people declined, it falls on the people.

outline.heading: We think about liability at work
outline.gist: Physicians, engineers, lawyers and contractors constantly ask whether they could be sued; why do we treat this world that way and not the Hereafter, the epitome of fairness?

outline.heading: No lawyer on that day
outline.gist: Here a good lawyer or careful wording can get you off, but there everything is replayed in full detail, and the earth, the sky and the tree that stood there will testify.

outline.heading: Your own organs will speak
outline.gist: Eyes, ears and skin bear witness against the liar, and the assumption that the Lord would not hold him to account is what ruined him; you cannot scramble the fabric of the universe and escape it.

outline.heading: Fairness in every moment
outline.gist: Allah covered every base by sending messenger after messenger with similar values; we too must be fair always, to those we once resembled and in speaking the truth when it costs us or a loved one.

outline.heading: No one enters the Fire feeling wronged
outline.gist: The most frightening fact about that day: people enter Hell sad and wishing for more, but not one of them feels oppressed.

9:23.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ لَا تَتَّخِذُوٓاْ ءَابَآءَكُمۡ وَإِخۡوَٰنَكُمۡ أَوۡلِيَآءَ إِنِ ٱسۡتَحَبُّواْ ٱلۡكُفۡرَ عَلَى ٱلۡإِيمَٰنِۚ وَمَن يَتَوَلَّهُم مِّنكُمۡ فَأُوْلَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلظَّٰلِمُونَ
9:23.en: O ye who believe! Choose not your fathers nor your brethren for friends if they take pleasure in disbelief rather than faith. Whoso of you taketh them for friends, such are wrong-doers

9:24.ar: قُلۡ إِن كَانَ ءَابَآؤُكُمۡ وَأَبۡنَآؤُكُمۡ وَإِخۡوَٰنُكُمۡ وَأَزۡوَٰجُكُمۡ وَعَشِيرَتُكُمۡ وَأَمۡوَٰلٌ ٱقۡتَرَفۡتُمُوهَا وَتِجَٰرَةࣱ تَخۡشَوۡنَ كَسَادَهَا وَمَسَٰكِنُ تَرۡضَوۡنَهَآ أَحَبَّ إِلَيۡكُم مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِۦ وَجِهَادࣲ فِي سَبِيلِهِۦ فَتَرَبَّصُواْ حَتَّىٰ يَأۡتِيَ ٱللَّهُ بِأَمۡرِهِۦۗ وَٱللَّهُ لَا يَهۡدِي ٱلۡقَوۡمَ ٱلۡفَٰسِقِينَ
9:24.en: Say: If your fathers, and your sons, and your brethren, and your wives, and your tribe, and the wealth ye have acquired, and merchandise for which ye fear that there will no sale, and dwellings ye desire are dearer to you than Allah and His messenger and striving in His way: then wait till Allah bringeth His command to pass. Allah guideth not wrongdoing folk

2:219.ar: ۞يَسۡـَٔلُونَكَ عَنِ ٱلۡخَمۡرِ وَٱلۡمَيۡسِرِۖ قُلۡ فِيهِمَآ إِثۡمࣱ كَبِيرࣱ وَمَنَٰفِعُ لِلنَّاسِ وَإِثۡمُهُمَآ أَكۡبَرُ مِن نَّفۡعِهِمَاۗ وَيَسۡـَٔلُونَكَ مَاذَا يُنفِقُونَۖ قُلِ ٱلۡعَفۡوَۗ كَذَٰلِكَ يُبَيِّنُ ٱللَّهُ لَكُمُ ٱلۡأٓيَٰتِ لَعَلَّكُمۡ تَتَفَكَّرُونَ
2:219.en: They question thee about strong drink and games of chance. Say: In both is great sin, and (some) utility for men; but the sin of them is greater than their usefulness. And they ask thee what they ought to spend. Say: that which is superfluous. Thus Allah maketh plain to you (His) revelations, that haply ye may reflect

9:111.ar: ۞إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ ٱشۡتَرَىٰ مِنَ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ أَنفُسَهُمۡ وَأَمۡوَٰلَهُم بِأَنَّ لَهُمُ ٱلۡجَنَّةَۚ يُقَٰتِلُونَ فِي سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ فَيَقۡتُلُونَ وَيُقۡتَلُونَۖ وَعۡدًا عَلَيۡهِ حَقࣰّ ا فِي ٱلتَّوۡرَىٰةِ وَٱلۡإِنجِيلِ وَٱلۡقُرۡءَانِۚ وَمَنۡ أَوۡفَىٰ بِعَهۡدِهِۦ مِنَ ٱللَّهِۚ فَٱسۡتَبۡشِرُواْ بِبَيۡعِكُمُ ٱلَّذِي بَايَعۡتُم بِهِۦۚ وَذَٰلِكَ هُوَ ٱلۡفَوۡزُ ٱلۡعَظِيمُ
9:111.en: Lo! Allah hath bought from the believers their lives and their wealth because the Garden will be theirs: they shall fight in the way of Allah and shall slay and be slain. It is a promise which is binding on Him in the Torah and the Gospel and the Qur'an. Who fulfilleth His covenant better than Allah? Rejoice then in your bargain that ye have made, for that is the supreme triumph

vejhCEZQ1rc.speaker: adnan
vejhCEZQ1rc.speaker_note: Ramadan Quranic Themes night at MWN; refers to his own 2024 khutbahs and to people who approach him as imam
vejhCEZQ1rc.title: Ramadan 2025 Night 9: Quranic Themes, Recipes for Success
vejhCEZQ1rc.one_line: Three Quranic recipes for success: pardon and low expectations with people (7:199-200), unity without dispute (8:46), and loving Allah above all (9:23-24).
vejhCEZQ1rc.summary: He presents the Quran's recurring lists of the qualities of the successful as recipes: each passage varies slightly, so there is more than one path, and a believer should pick one passage and hold himself to it daily. The first recipe, from 7:199-200, governs dealings with people: accept whatever people can offer and keep expectations low, make pardon a way of life except in the face of oppression, which must be resisted, encourage good customs, walk away from the ignorant without arguing, and seek refuge in Allah when Shaytan stirs anger. He applies low expectations to marriage and recounts how hostile people repeatedly became friends and volunteers. The second, from 8:46, is communal: obey Allah and His Messenger and do not dispute, since disagreement is human but tanazu' means parting ways, and it brings failure and lost momentum. He points to divided Muslim communities in Canadian cities and to two billion Muslims unable to stop the massacre in Gaza, urging the young to feel urgency. The third, from 9:23-24, is of the heart: family, wealth, homes and businesses may be loved, but never more than Allah, His Prophet and striving for Him, as Abu Lahab's story shows.

outline.heading: The Quran's recurring recipes for success
outline.gist: Passages describing the people of Jannah vary slightly, and following any one set of these qualities leads to success.

outline.heading: Advice people wish they had followed
outline.gist: Successful people often recommend what they regret not doing, so weigh their advice carefully.

outline.heading: Keep the company of achievers
outline.gist: Success breeds success; reading the Quran puts you in the company of Allah and the prophets and the advice they lived by.

outline.heading: No single recipe, but common lines
outline.gist: The variation shows there is more than one way to succeed, while salah, zakah and humility recur in nearly every list.

outline.heading: Choose one passage and hold yourself to it
outline.gist: Pick at least one recipe and check every day whether you are meeting its milestones.

outline.heading: Al-Anfal as a recipe for a nation's success
outline.gist: The whole surah, with its laws of victory, describes the success of an ummah, which is why this theme suits tonight's portion.

outline.heading: Quranic themes as the canvas of the Quran
outline.gist: Any theme can be traced through any night's verses because these themes are the underlying maxims the Quran teaches throughout.

outline.heading: Take what people can give
outline.gist: Al-'afw means accepting whatever people offer; the lower your expectations, the happier, kinder and calmer you become.

outline.heading: Pardon as a way of life
outline.gist: The second meaning is to live by forgiving and not carrying grudges over others' harsh words or misjudgments.

outline.heading: No pardon while oppression continues
outline.gist: When rights or land are taken, forgiving is weakness that invites more oppression; reclaim your rights first, then forgive if you wish.

outline.heading: Two words, a whole lifestyle
outline.gist: In ordinary daily friction, when people are rude or unkind, let it go and move on.

outline.heading: Low expectations in marriage
outline.gist: Most marriages fail because both spouses expect too much; when expectations are low, every kindness becomes a bonus and happiness is the baseline.

outline.heading: Only Allah never disappoints
outline.gist: People will always disappoint you; hold high expectations only of those who ask you to mentor them.

outline.heading: Turn away from the ignorant
outline.gist: After encouraging good customs, do not argue with people who only seek your mistakes; let them finish and walk away, since most happiness is choosing your battles.

outline.heading: Answering bizarre comments with a dua
outline.gist: Faced with requests so strange he cannot begin to answer, he blesses the person and avoids the conversation next time.

outline.heading: Seek refuge when Shaytan kindles anger
outline.gist: When the urge rises to expose someone's ignorance, seek refuge in Allah, who hears and knows, from anger you will regret.

outline.heading: Hostile people who came around
outline.gist: Following this recipe, many who once despised him later became friends, congregants and volunteers; he restates its four parts.

outline.heading: A communal recipe: obey Allah and His Messenger
outline.gist: Unlike the first, personal recipe, this one concerns the ummah's success and begins with obedience.

outline.heading: Disagreement is human, dispute is not
outline.gist: Tanazu' is not differing in opinion but tearing unity apart until people refuse to work together.

outline.heading: The ummah is short on time
outline.gist: Other nations move fast toward their goals; the young must develop an urgency his generation lacked, with 75 years of occupation as the measure.

outline.heading: Failure and lost momentum
outline.gist: Disputes bring failure and make the ummah's wind stop blowing, the momentum people need to serve their community.

outline.heading: Divided Muslim communities in the West
outline.gist: Muslims in Western cities achieve little because leaders run small silos and will not sit together and plan.

outline.heading: Persevere to keep unity
outline.gist: Avoiding dispute is hard when dealing with difficult people, but Allah is with those who persevere, as the Prophet did.

outline.heading: Two billion Muslims could not stop a massacre
outline.gist: A quarter of humanity agrees on the sanctity of the holy land yet could not stop fifteen months of killing; the missing piece is unity.

outline.heading: Do not take hostile relatives as allies
outline.gist: Keep showing parents kindness whatever they do, but do not make relatives who work against your faith your closest allies.

outline.heading: The eight beloved things
outline.gist: Fathers, children, brothers, spouses, tribe, wealth, homes and businesses, if any is more beloved than Allah, His Messenger and striving for Him.

outline.heading: An explicit threat over what you love most
outline.gist: This is a matter of love in the heart, not decision-making, and unlike the Quran's many implied warnings, this threat is explicit.

outline.heading: Love them, just not more
outline.gist: All eight are things you are expected or commanded to love; the problem is comparison, not essence.

outline.heading: Passion for the deen like for a sick child
outline.gist: Nothing will change until our passion for Islam and the ummah at least matches what we feel for a sick child.

outline.heading: The ingredients must be right
outline.gist: Love for Allah must outweigh everything else combined, or one day the heavier love wins and you cannot give your life and wealth for Him.

outline.heading: Abu Lahab loved the Prophet, but not most
outline.gist: He celebrated the Prophet's birth and engaged his sons to his daughters, yet loved his wealth and status more.

outline.heading: Beware what you let yourself love
outline.gist: Love can be shaped indirectly with finesse; he recalls the three recipes for etiquette, unity and the heart.

outline.heading: Outro

BMsih8FnXaw.title: Ramadan Reminders 1446: Part 1, The Opportunity
BMsih8FnXaw.one_line: Ramadan is the greatest opportunity Allah offers, given only to those who value it; renew intentions, keep knocking and avoid distractions.
BMsih8FnXaw.summary: Around the point in Ramadan when masjid attendance always starts to dip, the sheikh offers an analogy: if you open a rare door for someone and watch them slack, you will not offer them the next opportunity, and nobody would blame you. Ramadan is Allah's opportunity, with Paradise open and your heart called to Him, and every job, scholarship or investment ranks far below it. Closeness to Allah, unlike worldly goods, is given only to those who value it and can be withdrawn when they stop, which is why many long for a connection they had when younger; it can still return with divine interest. His first reminder, repeated every year, is to revise your intention daily, since good intention covers shortcomings. Allah's commodity is expensive: as a sixteen-year-old in Syria he crossed an hour of transit to his Quran teacher, was sent home three times, and was taught only after returning a fourth time, because the teacher had to know he wanted it. Embrace the fatigue as reward. In the second khutbah he warns against small distractions, especially phones and social media, urges men to prioritise Fajr and Isha in congregation, and ends with the hadith that Allah comes faster to those who approach Him.

outline.heading: Opening
The dip in the Ramadan graph
outline.gist: Around this point every year attendance starts to fall and full masjids thin out. But Ramadan is not its first or last few days; it is a whole-month opportunity.

outline.heading: Waste an opportunity and the giver moves on
outline.gist: If you work to get someone a job or scholarship they could never get alone and watch them slack, you will quietly give the next chance to someone else, even if you did it for Allah, and nobody would blame you.

outline.heading: Ramadan: Allah's opportunity
outline.gist: Allah has the highest example. One month in twelve He opens Paradise, closes Hell and calls your heart to know and connect with Him; nothing in life comes close.

outline.heading: Every other opportunity is a distant second
outline.gist: Picture the scholarship, admission, job or investment you most want: all rank far below the chance for your heart to connect with Allah. If you do not see it that way, you will not get it.

outline.heading: Meat for someone with no teeth
outline.gist: Allah gives worldly things even to people who do not value them, as the Arabic proverb puts it. What pains him most is a gifted intellect wasted.

outline.heading: His closeness, only for those who value it
outline.gist: Drawing near to Allah is hard, and His closeness and love are given only to those who understand their worth. Stop valuing the connection and He takes it back.

outline.heading: Lost closeness can return with interest
outline.gist: Many look back on a younger self who felt close to Allah and cannot find it again. It can come back better than before, with divine interest, once you show Him it matters most.

outline.heading: Show Him this is the best offer you have had
outline.gist: Show Allah you would not trade these days of fasting and nights of prayer for anything. The two-week waterfall in attendance reveals hearts missing what He offers.

outline.heading: Reminder one: revise your intentions
outline.gist: Those who are on call or truly cannot attend still get the full reward. Ramadan is won by intention, and good intention makes up for weak action.

outline.heading: Intention carries you through stumbling
outline.gist: Keep revising daily and recall what you asked for at the start: freedom from punishment, Paradise without reckoning, being with your family, repentance and a mended heart.

outline.heading: Knock on the only door that can give it
outline.gist: If you have not received it yet, come for every prayer and keep knocking, for years if needed. No one else owns these things to give; Allah's commodity is expensive, and it is Paradise.

outline.heading: Sent home three times in Damascus
outline.gist: At 16 he left school early, waited for buses and walked uphill in his military-style uniform to reach his Quran teacher, who sent him home three times. When he wanted to quit, his father said it was not up for negotiation.

outline.heading: I needed to know you wanted it
outline.gist: On the fourth visit he was accepted, and the man is still his teacher. Asked why, the teacher said he had to see he truly wanted it; Allah's gift is no different.

outline.heading: Keep knocking, Ramadan after Ramadan
outline.gist: What Allah offers is priceless, so prove you want it. It may not come in the first, tenth or twentieth Ramadan; knocking for two days and returning on the 27th night does not work.

outline.heading: Bathe in the fatigue
outline.gist: Embrace the exhaustion: you are tired only because of fasting and night prayer, not a late show or a holiday, and every bit of it is being banked as reward.

outline.heading: Interlude
The final reminder: beware of distractions
outline.gist: Shaytan is chained but left distractions behind. The ego hates serious things, so we procrastinate with trivia; small distractions add up.

outline.heading: Phones and screens drain the month's baraka
outline.gist: Are the social media apps still on your phone? Images that are borderline or worse, and hours of worthless screen time, pull your mind from the beauty of the month.

outline.heading: Lost through small mistakes
outline.gist: People rarely lose everything through one catastrophe; a chain of small bad decisions strips time of its baraka. For men, praying in congregation must take priority.

outline.heading: The heavy, cold prayers first
outline.gist: Fajr and Isha are the heavy prayers, and showing up when it is cold is true commitment. Then pray taraweeh and push past your habits, since you are asking for what you can never deserve.

outline.heading: Fathers who watch their gifts ignored
outline.gist: Most conflict between parents and children comes from fathers who wear themselves out for opportunities their children do not value. Seeing an opportunity used makes the giver give more.

outline.heading: Show Him you are serious
outline.gist: Do not give up at the first difficulty; come back tomorrow and the day after. Whoever comes to Allah a little, He comes twice as far.

outline.heading: Outro

Be0O0mMvt44.title: Tazkiyah Pearls 4: Four Daily Focuses
Be0O0mMvt44.one_line: Four things every Muslim should reflect on daily until second nature: servanthood, ihsan, the acceptance of deeds, and intention.
Be0O0mMvt44.summary: He sets out four focuses that every Muslim on the path of tazkiyah should bring to mind at least once a day until they become second nature. First, servanthood: you are a servant of Allah, the first thing you will be questioned about, and you must work out for yourself what that means by asking whether each choice befits a good servant. Like a keen janitor who barges into board meetings, good intentions without understanding your role earn no thanks. Titles and roles are only extensions of that service. Second, ihsan: every deed has an outward form and an inner side, as when charity is given lawfully but also without demeaning anyone or seeking self-gratification, and routine erodes this awareness. Third, the acceptance of deeds: every good deed remains pending, Allah rejects deeds shared with partners and those spoiled by bad etiquette with the Prophet, so acting entitled to reward is arrogant, while healthy worry raises both quantity and quality. Fourth, intention: it can never be perfect but can always improve, illustrated by an early scholar who paused before a funeral to set his intention and by the rule that swimming without intending ghusl does not count. He asks listeners to memorise the four and review them daily.

outline.heading: Four daily focuses that must become second nature
outline.gist: Distinct from formal contemplation, these are four aspects of the relationship with Allah to recall at least daily until they become automatic.

outline.heading: Focus: reaffirming servanthood
outline.gist: Ask daily how you are doing as a servant of Allah and whether your thoughts and choices reflect it; you must define it for yourself, and it is the first question you face.

outline.heading: The enthusiastic janitor in the boardroom
outline.gist: An employee who loves the company but ignores his actual job is scorned, not thanked; understanding your role as a servant is not demeaning but takes time.

outline.heading: The Prophet as the true servant
outline.gist: Allah honoured the Prophet with the title of servant; keep asking whether a good servant would speak, act or react this way.

outline.heading: At least show you cared
outline.gist: Even if you fall short, you can stand before Allah having asked yourself the question every day and tried your best.

outline.heading: Focus: ihsan, the inner side of every deed
outline.gist: Every act has an apparent form and a hidden side of sincerity and closeness to Allah; ihsan is doing it with excellence.

outline.heading: Charity, school and the inner questions
outline.gist: Give a reasonable amount without demeaning the recipient, but also ask why you gave, whether to gratify the ego or out of gratitude; every daily act has this dimension.

outline.heading: Routine drains meaning from deeds
outline.gist: Forgetting the inner side turns actions into routine that loses its joy.

outline.heading: Focus: every deed is pending acceptance
outline.gist: If this never keeps you up at night you have not understood it; anyone certain of one accepted deed would need nothing more.

outline.heading: A rejected deed is the scariest outcome
outline.gist: Worse than not acting is acting and having it refused; Allah needs no partner and leaves a deed shared with another.

outline.heading: Deeds nullified by poor etiquette with the Prophet
outline.gist: The Quran warns that raising voices over the Prophet's can void deeds without one noticing, and the theme of acceptance recurs throughout the Quran.

outline.heading: Good assumption without entitlement
outline.gist: We hope Allah accepts, but He promised general rewards, not a guarantee for each of our deeds; acting certain is arrogance and bad etiquette.

outline.heading: Concern raises both quantity and quality
outline.gist: Worrying about acceptance makes you do more and better; the righteous hoped for even one accepted prostration, though Allah sends signs of acceptance.

outline.heading: You are a servant, everything else is a role
outline.gist: Leader, doctor or teacher are only roles for serving Him; on the Day all titles vanish and only your name and your parent's remain.

outline.heading: Wearing the goggles of ihsan
outline.gist: What matters is whether Allah approves the quality of a prayer, not whether people admire it; acting as if acceptance were guaranteed is disrespectful.

outline.heading: Focus: intention can improve but never be perfect
outline.gist: Only the Prophet's soul had perfect intentions; ours can be refined a little more each time.

outline.heading: The scholar who paused before a funeral
outline.gist: A great early scholar sat for a minute before joining a janazah to correct his intention, shaming students who assumed theirs were obviously right.

outline.heading: Without intention the deed did not happen
outline.gist: Intention is the first condition of any act in fiqh; swimming in the purest water without intending ghusl leaves you still needing it.

outline.heading: Ask why you do each thing
outline.gist: Question your motives for work, school, prayer and fasting, watching for social pressure or self-gratification; formal reflection can start at five minutes.

outline.heading: Review of the four focuses
outline.gist: Servanthood, ihsan, acceptance and intention must be reviewed daily until they run automatically and show in ethics and behaviour.

outline.heading: Outro
